result.what_interviewer_wanted: Explain Docker’s purpose, benefits, and how it solves environment consistency, with a brief mention of best practices like Dockerfile structure and secret handling.
result.improved_answer: Docker packages an application with its dependencies into an image, and a container is a running instance of that image. This lets the app run the same on my laptop, in CI, and on the server, eliminating the “works on my machine” problem. I build images from a slim Python base, cache dependencies by copying requirements first, then add the code. In my FastAPI project I used this approach so teammates could run the service with a single command, and I kept secrets out of the image by passing them as environment variables.
